newsitem.title: USA: Mild early morning earthquake jolts Los Angeles.
newsitem.headline: Mild early morning earthquake jolts Los Angeles.

text.p: Some residents of Los Angeles were jolted out of their beds early on Friday by an earthquake which caused minor damage but no apparent injuries.

A spokesman for the California Institute of Technology said the earthquake, which struck shortly before 1.30 a.m. PST (0930 GMT), had a magnitude of 3.3 on the open-ended Richter scale and was centred on the Inglewood fault south of the downtown area.
Residents reported pictures falling off walls and ornaments tumbling from shelves. Minor cracks appeared in some houses, but there were no reports of major damage.
The earthquake was followed about five minutes later by a smaller aftershock.
Caltech seismologist Nick Scheckel said the temblor was a fresh earthquake and not an aftershock.
The Los Angeles Fire Department went into an "earthquake mode," moving all of its vehicles onto the streets, but a spokesman said it was purely a precautionary measure.
